# #705 — pre-push gate diffs against origin/main, so every wip-branch lane inherits 80 commits of Python attribution

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-10T00:46:43Z
Updated: 2026-08-10T01:36:51Z
Closed: 2026-08-10T01:36:51Z

---

## What happens

`_githooks/pre-push` decides whether a push touched the Python packages by
diffing against `origin/main`. Every lane in the current flow branches from
`wip/2026-08-07`, which is **80 commits ahead of `origin/main`**. So the hook
attributes all 80 commits' Python changes to whatever lane is pushing.

Measured on lane `lane/issue-artifacts-outcomes` (2026-08-09), which changes
zero Python files:

```
git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) HEAD -- python/openbrain | wc -l
# => 1     (what the hook believes the push changed)

git diff --name-only origin/wip/2026-08-07 HEAD -- python/openbrain | wc -l
# => 0     (what the push actually changed)
```

The hook then runs `uv run pytest -q` for `python/openbrain` and fails the push
on `test_receipts_gate_crosslang.py::test_python_capture_receipt_clears_the_gates_capture_block`
— which is **#704**, a known main-owned failure that reproduces on the
unmodified base commit `a45e7d9` in a separate checkout.

Net effect: a lane whose diff contains no Python is blocked by a Python test it
did not touch, inherited from five commits already on the wip branch.

## Where

Both base-selection paths hardcode `origin/main`:

- `_githooks/pre-push:32-37` — the stdin-range path, taken when the branch is
  new (`remote_sha` is the zero SHA), which is every first lane push.
- `_githooks/pre-push:59-65` — the manual-invocation path.

## Why it matters beyond the annoyance

The gate stops discriminating. Once every lane is told it changed the Python
package, a push that genuinely breaks Python looks exactly like one that
touched only markdown, and the honest response to the failure ("not mine")
becomes the habitual one. That is how a gate turns into noise that gets
routed around with `--no-verify` — which the lane contract forbids, correctly.

## Suggested direction (not implemented here)

Compare against the branch's actual integration target rather than a hardcoded
`origin/main`: the configured upstream (`@{upstream}`) when one exists, else
the merge-base with the branch the PR targets. Whatever is chosen should be
announced in the hook's output — "comparing against X" — so a future lane can
see which base produced the verdict instead of inferring it from a failure.

Filed from the artifact-resolution lane, which hit it on a zero-Python diff.
State: WRITTEN (defect confirmed by the two measurements above); no fix
proposed in code yet.

## Discussion (1)

### rodaddy — 2026-08-10T01:36:51Z

Fixed by PR #708, squash-merged into `wip/2026-08-07` as `e3917ab`.

**What changed.** `_githooks/pre-push` had the base hardcoded to `origin/main` in TWO places (the stdin-range path and the manual path). Base selection now lives in one `resolve_base` function called from both, choosing the branch's configured upstream and falling back to `origin/main` → `main` → the empty tree. The chosen base and the resulting per-package flags are ANNOUNCED, which the issue asked for by name.

**Attribution correction, announced not silently fixed.** This issue's body names `python/openbrain-memory`, but the file inherited from the wip branch is in the sibling package `python/openbrain`, whose gate owns the `test_receipts_gate_crosslang.py` failure. Same defect, corrected package.

**Two extra defects the suggested direction did not anticipate**, both found because the fix was driven on the real path rather than only through its test seam:

- `@{upstream}` was first keyed on the TIP, and git hands a pre-push hook a raw SHA. `<sha>@{upstream}` is meaningless, so the lookup returned empty and fell through to origin/main — silently, in exactly the direction this issue is about.
- `@{upstream}` takes a SHORT BRANCH NAME. git sends the FULL ref, and `refs/heads/x@{upstream}` is a hard `fatal: no such branch`, indistinguishable from "no upstream configured" and falling through the same way.

**Live proof (RUNNING).** The lane's own push, through the fixed hook:

```
  base: origin/wip/2026-08-07 — configured upstream
  changed: python/openbrain-memory=no python/openbrain=no parity=no
  Python package unchanged; skipping Python package gate
  openbrain package unchanged; skipping openbrain package gate
pre-push: all checks passed ✓
 * [new branch]      lane/fix-gates-705-706 -> lane/fix-gates-705-706
```

The pre-fix hook, on that same zero-Python branch, announced nothing, reported `openbrain package changed`, and failed on `test_python_capture_receipt_clears_the_gates_capture_block` (#704) — this issue's symptom, reproduced and then fixed. No `--no-verify` at any point.

**Done-means.** `scripts/done-means/705-pre-push-base-selection.sh`, six clauses, written RED-first and re-proven RED against the pre-fix hook with the final clause set. Clause (f) drives a real stdin range with a zero remote SHA and is the only clause that catches either `@{upstream}` defect — clauses (a)-(e) all passed against the broken version because they used the `--explain` seam. Mutation-tested: forcing the flags to `no` makes clause (b) fail, so silencing the gate cannot pass.

**Residual, stated:** `core.hooksPath` is an absolute path to the primary checkout, so a lane worktree runs the PRIMARY checkout's pre-push. Now that this is merged to `wip/2026-08-07`, lanes based on it get the fixed selection. Recorded in `docs/sme/entries/2026-08-09-a-gate-that-judges-from-a-tree-other-than-the-one-under-review.md` and lane-contract round 28.
